title: Norwest pushes deeper into AI with new $4B fund
slides: Can Norwest's $4B fund outsmart AI's boom?
It's the firm's largest fund ever raised
But most AI startups don't need venture capital
Founders can now raise larger early checks from one firm
Ask: does more money mean better AI outcomes?
thread_text:
1. The $4B question

Norwest just closed its largest fund ever — and it's aimed straight at the AI boom. With so much capital chasing so few deals, the real test isn't raising it.

2. Why now, why so big

Venture firms are racing to write bigger early checks before rounds get crowded out. One firm can now lead a startup from seed to Series B alone.

3. Most AI startups don't need it

Many AI tools can ship and earn revenue without a single venture dollar. That gap between fund size and actual need is where the tension lives.

4. Founders get more leverage

Less dilution, faster decisions, one relationship instead of four. But bigger checks can also push founders to spend before the product is ready.

5. Test your own thesis

Pick an AI startup you use. Would a $20M check make it better, or just bigger? Write your answer down — then watch what Norwest backs next.

instagram.caption:
Norwest just raised the biggest fund in its history — $4 billion aimed straight at AI.

It's a bet that one firm can now lead a startup from seed to Series B alone, handing founders bigger early checks and less dilution. 💰

The catch: plenty of AI tools ship and earn revenue without a single venture dollar. 🤔 More money doesn't automatically mean better AI — and big checks can push founders to spend before the product is ready.

If you build with AI, cheaper capital and faster decisions could reach you sooner than you think. ⚡
